title: Add defaults proposals: record, validation, status listing, apply check
summary: Build step 3 of defaults-loop.md §12: from introspection records (cases) it clusters by failure class, and at N distinct jobs writes an athena.defaults-proposal/1 record validated with DefaultsModel::parse and the evidence-after-decision rule. `athena status` lists open proposals with sources. Accepting one makes an ordinary job with defaults.toml as a deliverable, checked against the proposal. Rejecting records a reason and suppresses the class until new evidence arrives. No Jev; tests use fixture records in a temp dir.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and tests are Rust.
Fixture-record tests in a temporary directory; cargo test passes and clippy is clean.
Behavior criteria name cargo test, clippy and fmt --check as the verifier's commands.
Follows the written design (§8, §9, §12) and updates §12 to mark step 3 built.
The 'never write defaults.toml' rule is enforced by a test on the module source, not prose.
One change limited to step 3; Jev, render measurement and expectations records are excluded.
Doc comments, design doc update and changelog entry written for an outside reader.
Threshold, record names and CLI shape recovered from the design doc and existing introspection code.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The repeat threshold N is a named constant in code (assumed 3 distinct jobs, per the §8.2 example), not a new athena.toml key, so no governance file changes.
Clustering uses the existing failure_class id on recorded introspections (Records.cases) with distinct job ids; no Jev matching.
The statement and applies_to are drafted by code from the class registry entry and the cases' cause text (no language model, no Jev); the user may edit them in the apply job.

Proposals are stored as a new schema athena.defaults-proposal/1 in athena-data records.rs under records/, written the way introspections are; status transitions (rejected, accepted with job) append a new record rather than mutate.

Accept is a new CLI path (athena accept-proposal <id> or similar) that submits an ordinary job request 'apply defaults proposal X' through the normal reading and acceptance flow; it never writes defaults.toml. The apply-as-a-job check is code that verifies the candidate defaults.toml: id and statement equal the proposal, version equals base plus one, and DefaultsModel::parse accepts it.
Reject is a CLI command taking a reason; suppression holds until a class has at least N more distinct jobs of cases newer than the rejection (design §9).
The §8 fields assumptions, signals and evidence (Jev probabilities) are omitted or empty in this step, since no Jev exists; the record notes this.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new athena.defaults-proposal/1 record type exists in athena-data with fields id, kind (add/amend), statement, applies_to, version {from,to}, sources (intervention/introspection ids with job ids), status (pending/accepted with job/rejected with reason/withdrawn) and candidate_sha256, and is registered in the record validation and schema listing.
Proposal generation code reads introspection cases, groups them by failure class, and proposes only when cases span at least N distinct jobs; N is a named constant.

Every proposal is validated by building a candidate defaults.toml and calling DefaultsModel::parse; the id must be unique among the model and pending proposals, the version bump is base plus one, and sources are checked with the existing evidence-after-decision rule.
No code in the proposal path opens defaults.toml for writing; a test asserts this on the module source.

Run `cargo test`: fixture-record tests in a temp dir show that (a) cases of one class across fewer than N jobs yield no proposal, (b) N distinct jobs yield one pending proposal citing those records, (c) repeats within the same job do not count, (d) a candidate that fails DefaultsModel::parse or cites evidence that postdates the decision is refused, (e) rejection suppresses the class until N newer distinct-job cases arrive, after which a proposal reappears.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows `athena status` (text and --json) lists open proposals with id, kind, statement, version bump and source records, and omits rejected and accepted ones.

Run `cargo test`: apply-check tests accept a candidate defaults.toml that matches the proposal and reject one with a wrong statement, wrong id, version not base+1, or a parse failure; accepting a proposal produces a job request listing defaults.toml as a deliverable instead of editing the file.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean. The design doc §12 step 3 is marked built with a short description, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

out_of_scope: Jev client, evaluate calls, matching or clustering by Jev (steps 5, 6)
Measuring render() with the live counter (step 4)
Writing athena.default-expectations/1 records or the assumptions/signals/evidence fields beyond what exists without Jev
Any direct write to defaults.toml by Athena; editing defaults.toml itself
Running over the real records/ directory
Changes to athena.toml, CI, or other governance files
departures: Larger than the reference: it adds a new record schema, clustering, validation, CLI commands, status output and an apply check across about 6 crates and files, so cost and time are well above the median and verification is less likely to pass first time.
